source.title: FADE: Why Bad Descriptions Happen to Good Features
source.authors: Bruno Puri; Aakriti Jain; Elena Golimblevskaia; Patrick Kahardipraja; Thomas Wiegand; W. Samek; S. Lapuschkin

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether neuron-feature descriptions align with activations on evaluation data and reports examples where descriptions miss parts of a feature’s activating behavior. This refines and qualitatively challenges the idea that descriptions derived from activating examples establish that a feature has been adequately explained; it does not measure the claimed Qwen3-32B pole shares.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates descriptions with Clarity, Responsiveness, Purity, and Faithfulness. Its results on descriptions of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2 neurons bear on V6 and V7. Results for SAEs and other description-generation settings were not treated as direct tests of the neuron-specific versions unless they provide a concrete example relevant to V6. Results cited from other work were not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: FADE checks whether descriptions written from top-activating examples predict where Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct neurons fire on held-out natural text (Responsiveness, Purity) and on synthetic text (Clarity). That bears directly on V6. It does not run simulation scoring itself, so V7 is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also stress that single-metric (simulation-based) evaluation gives incomplete or misleading descriptions, and that describing SAE features is harder than describing MLP neurons. They also find that larger explainers and more examples improve descriptions.
record.recipe_differences: Rather than auditing pole-level job counts, FADE evaluates feature-description alignment using synthetic samples, rated natural samples, activation specificity, and steering-based Faithfulness.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer affects reported Gemma-2 scores; the study also reports variation with description-generation choices, including explainer model, number of examples, and sample count. For layer 20, the authors note possible Faithfulness bias from tuning MaxAct* on that layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering Gemma-2-2b neurons barely increases concept-related output (mean Faithfulness 0.009-0.025), versus about 0.17 for Gemma Scope SAE features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neuron descriptions derived from activations rarely predict the neuron's causal effect on output.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features have higher Purity but lower Clarity than Gemma-2 neurons, and larger SAEs are harder to describe.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features are more monosemantic than neurons, but harder to describe precisely.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 2025
record.problems: The study evaluates only selected features and layers rather than establishing a population-wide share. The evaluation relies on LLM-generated ratings and synthetic data; the authors note dataset-coverage and evaluator-bias limitations. No uncertainty estimates for the reported metric values are given, and the text does not specify a threshold defining a good score for the V7 proportion.
record.rows_left_out: SAE size comparisons, SAE-only prompt/sample-count experiments, and other non-neuron description-generation comparisons were not extracted as direct neuron-version results. The paper also reports additional qualitative examples and cites earlier studies; cited results were excluded.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B pole audit or shares.
No pole-share estimates across models or scale.
Explainer-model and prompt comparisons are on SAEs. The cause of messy neurons is not tested.
No prevalence share of neurons whose explanations fail. Only two neuron models and a few layers.
FADE does not score explanations by simulating activations. The simulation scores shown are Choi et al.'s, and no fraction of neurons with good scores is reported.

missing.what: Gemma-2 neuron results for delimiter vs numeric prompts (Purity 0.61 vs 0.64) and for 5/15/50 samples (Purity 0.59-0.62): more examples help only slightly.
Distributions of Clarity, Responsiveness and Purity for Llama neurons with Choi vs MaxAct* descriptions (figure only, no numbers).

record.verdict_notes: Only means are tabled, and the authors warn of high variance. Faithfulness means are deflated because Faithfulness is set to 0 unless Clarity and Responsiveness are at least 0.5. MaxAct* prompts were tuned on Gemma-2 layer 20. The 0.77 for feature 5183 is Transluce's own simulation score, not a FADE result.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or counts of neuron poles by number of jobs or understood status.
No comparable pole-share estimates across models, dense and MoE architectures, or trillion-parameter models.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron analysis or test of pose/recursive generalization.
The study compares layers and explanation-generation settings, but does not test the claimed causal account or the InceptionV1-sized estimates.
No attribution-graph or circuit reconstruction test.
The study evaluates selected features and descriptions, not a systematic prevalence estimate across neurons; it does not test every way explanations may be written.
The study reports multiple automated alignment metrics and examples, but does not report the fraction of neurons exceeding a defined good-score threshold or test the claim’s stated proportion.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: FADE reevaluation of descriptions from Choi et al. and comparison with MaxAct* descriptions

conditions.value: subsampled features and top 10% selected by the simulated-activation metric

rows.baseline: Average results across all subsampled features for comparison with top 10%
rows.value: The top 10% yields only a marginal gain in Clarity and Responsiveness, while Purity worsens; MaxAct* has slightly lower Clarity but significantly higher Responsiveness and Purity.
rows.note: The study reports these qualitative comparisons but the supplied text does not give the figure’s metric values.
rows.check: Descriptions with high simulation scores (Choi et al.) still get low Purity. Top-10% selection by simulation makes Purity worse. Not V7: it shows simulation scores overstating quality, not a minority scoring well. Values are figure-only.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: FADE evaluation of feature 5183 description and activating pattern

conditions.value: Transluce description from Choi et al.

rows.measure: Purity and alignment of the description with the feature’s activating pattern
rows.baseline: Compared with the MaxAct* description for the same feature
rows.value: The description has near-zero Purity; the authors state that the feature responds to multiple distinct concepts, including names, “is” in specific contexts, and coding patterns.

rows.note: The paper says the description has a relatively high metric score of 0.77 in Transluce’s evaluation, but does not identify that value as a FADE metric. The MaxAct* description has lower Clarity and Responsiveness but higher Purity.
rows.check: The Transluce description scores 0.77 in Transluce's simulation-based evaluation but has near-zero FADE Purity. The neuron is polysemantic (names, 'is', code).

source_check.notes: The text extraction drops superscripts: '103' is 10^3. Experiments use 1,000 randomly chosen features per layer and the top 1,000 activating samples. Table 3 values are means with high variance, and MaxAct* was tuned on layer 20. Llama top-10% values appear only in Figure 3. 0.77 for feature 5183 is Transluce's simulation-based score, not a FADE metric.

statements.correction: Clarity: synthetic samples generated from the description. Responsiveness and Purity: gpt-4o-mini ratings of natural Pile test-partition samples, scored with the Gini coefficient and Average Precision. 0.77 is the score from Transluce's (Choi et al.) simulated-activation evaluation, not a FADE metric.
statements.problem: The FADE numbers are right: layer 12 Clarity/Responsiveness/Purity 0.44/0.54/0.43, and feature 5183 has 0.77 in Transluce's (simulation-based) evaluation with near-zero Purity. But the conditions call FADE's measure 'synthetic-sample ratings'. Only Clarity uses synthetic samples. Responsiveness and Purity use LLM-rated natural samples.

statements.correction: 10^3 (1,000) randomly chosen features per layer, not 103. MaxAct* prompts were tuned on Gemma-2-2b layer 20 and applied to layers 3 and 25. Layers 3/20/25: Responsiveness 0.71/0.74/0.65, Purity 0.55/0.61/0.54. On Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct L19, MaxAct* has slightly lower Clarity but significantly higher Responsiveness and Purity than Choi et al.
statements.problem: Ranges are right (Responsiveness 0.65-0.74, Purity 0.54-0.61), and MaxAct* gives much higher Purity than Choi's descriptions on Llama. But the conditions give '103 random features per layer'. The text's '103' is a lost superscript for 10^3. The tuning is already qualified in the conditions ('tuned on layer 20').

statements.correction: Gemma-2-2b Purity by layer: 3: 0.55, 12: 0.43, 20: 0.61 (MaxAct* tuned on this layer), 25: 0.54. Faithfulness 0.009/0.016/0.011/0.025.
statements.problem: Minor: the claim that layer 12 is worst and layer 20 best holds for Clarity, Responsiveness and Purity. Faithfulness is highest at layer 25 and lowest at layer 3, all at most 0.025. The statement already marks layer 20 as tuned.
